\section[cognitiō, cognitiōnis]{cognitiō, cognitiōnis — an inquiry, a hearing; knowledge}

\label{lesson:LA-C412-cognitio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for a promise to appear in court, then the Latin for a legal expert.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: cognitiō, cognitiōnis}
\textbf{cognitiō, cognitiōnis} — \textquotedblleft{}an inquiry, a hearing; knowledge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cōnsul cognitiōnem dē caede habuit.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The consul held an inquiry into the murder.}
\end{quote}

\emph{cognitiō, cognitiōnis} f., built on \emph{cognōscō}: getting to know, and a judge's hearing of a case. English \emph{cognition}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cognitiō} is the noun built on \emph{cognitus}, the participle of \emph{cognōscō} \textquotedblleft{}to get to know\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short). English \emph{cognition} comes from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cognitiō, cognitiōnis}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cognitiō, cognitiōnis}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{cognitiō, cognitiōnis}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for a promise to appear in court, then the Latin for a legal expert, then say \emph{cognitiō, cognitiōnis} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does cognitiō, cognitiōnis mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An inquiry, a hearing; knowledge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[quaesītor, quaesītōris]{quaesītor, quaesītōris — an investigator; a presiding judge}

\label{lesson:LA-C412-quaesitor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for a legal expert, then the Latin for an inquiry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: quaesītor, quaesītōris}
\textbf{quaesītor, quaesītōris} — \textquotedblleft{}an investigator; a presiding judge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Quaesītor testēs audīvit.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The investigator heard the witnesses.}
\end{quote}

\emph{quaesītor, quaesītōris} m., built on \emph{quaerō}, to seek, to inquire.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{quaesītor} is built on \emph{quaerō} \textquotedblleft{}to seek, to inquire\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short), from its participle \emph{quaesītus}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[interrogō, interrogāre]{interrogō, interrogāre — to question, to examine}

\label{lesson:LA-C412-interrogo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for an inquiry, then the Latin for an investigator.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: interrogō, interrogāre}
\textbf{interrogō, interrogāre} — \textquotedblleft{}to question, to examine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Iūdex testem interrogāvit.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The judge questioned the witness.}
\end{quote}

\emph{interrogō, interrogāre, interrogāvī, interrogātum}, \emph{inter} + \emph{rogō}. English \emph{interrogate}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{interrogō} is built from \emph{inter} \textquotedblleft{}between\textquotedblright{} and \emph{rogō} \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short). English \emph{interrogate} comes from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[dēlātor, dēlātōris]{dēlātor, dēlātōris — an informer, an accuser}

\label{lesson:LA-C412-delator}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for an investigator, then the Latin for to question.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dēlātor, dēlātōris}
\textbf{dēlātor, dēlātōris} — \textquotedblleft{}an informer, an accuser\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dēlātōrēs multōs innocentēs accūsāvērunt.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Informers accused many innocent people.}
\end{quote}

\emph{dēlātor, dēlātōris} m., built on the verb for reporting a name to a magistrate. Under the emperors, informers could grow rich.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dēlātor} is built on \emph{dēlātum}, the supine of \emph{dēferō} \textquotedblleft{}to carry down, to report\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): one who reports a name. English \emph{delator} comes from it (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis]{dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis — a defence}

\label{lesson:LA-C412-defensio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for to question, then the Latin for an informer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis}
\textbf{dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis} — \textquotedblleft{}a defence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dēfēnsiō reī longa fuit.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The defence of the accused was long.}
\end{quote}

\emph{dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis} f., the noun of \emph{dēfendō}. English \emph{defence} comes through French from the same verb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dēfēnsiō} is the noun built on \emph{dēfendō} \textquotedblleft{}to ward off, to defend\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). English \emph{defence} comes through French from the same verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 405–412 — a review}

\label{lesson:LA-R412-review-405-412}



\begin{quote}
Say the Latin for a counting board and a pebble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a counting board, a pebble, to count out, to say repeatedly, a task
  \item clever, attentive, slow, painstaking, careless
  \item knowledge, understanding, teaching, ignorance, to imitate
  \item a mistake, a fault, a cane, a lash, to be beaten
  \item an edict, a decree, a rule, lawful, allowed
  \item a bill, to publish, to repeal, to make sacred and binding, to lay down
  \item the judgement seat, a lawsuit, to go to law, a promise to appear in court, a legal expert
  \item an inquiry, an investigator, to question, an informer, a defence
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A counting board? (\textbf{abacus, abacī}.) A pebble? (\textbf{calculus, calculī}.) To count out? (\textbf{ēnumerō, ēnumerāre}.) To say repeatedly? (\textbf{dictō, dictāre}.) A task? (\textbf{pēnsum, pēnsī}.) Clever? (\textbf{ingeniōsus, ingeniōsa, ingeniōsum}.) Attentive? (\textbf{attentus, attenta, attentum}.) Slow? (\textbf{tardus, tarda, tardum}.) Painstaking? (\textbf{sēdulus, sēdula, sēdulum}.) Careless? (\textbf{neglegēns, neglegentis}.) Knowledge? (\textbf{scientia, scientiae}.) Understanding? (\textbf{intellegentia, intellegentiae}.) Teaching? (\textbf{doctrīna, doctrīnae}.) Ignorance? (\textbf{īnscītia, īnscītiae}.) To imitate? (\textbf{imitor, imitārī}.) A mistake? (\textbf{mendum, mendī}.) A fault? (\textbf{vitium, vitiī}.) A cane? (\textbf{ferula, ferulae}.) A lash? (\textbf{verber, verberis}.) To be beaten? (\textbf{vāpulō, vāpulāre}.) An edict? (\textbf{ēdictum, ēdictī}.) A decree? (\textbf{dēcrētum, dēcrētī}.) A rule? (\textbf{praeceptum, praeceptī}.) Lawful? (\textbf{lēgitimus, lēgitima, lēgitimum}.) Allowed? (\textbf{licitus, licita, licitum}.) A bill? (\textbf{rogātiō, rogātiōnis}.) To publish? (\textbf{prōmulgō, prōmulgāre}.) To repeal? (\textbf{abrogō, abrogāre}.) To make sacred and binding? (\textbf{sanciō, sancīre}.) To lay down? (\textbf{praescrībō, praescrībere}.) The judgement seat? (\textbf{tribūnal, tribūnālis}.) A lawsuit? (\textbf{līs, lītis}.) To go to law? (\textbf{lītigō, lītigāre}.) A promise to appear in court? (\textbf{vadimōnium, vadimōniī}.) A legal expert? (\textbf{iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī}.) An inquiry? (\textbf{cognitiō, cognitiōnis}.) An investigator? (\textbf{quaesītor, quaesītōris}.) To question? (\textbf{interrogō, interrogāre}.) An informer? (\textbf{dēlātor, dēlātōris}.) A defence? (\textbf{dēfēnsiō, dēfēnsiōnis}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
